extraction_accuracy.findings: Most extracted fields are supported by the transcript. Claim Number, Policy Number, Location of Loss, Police Report Number, Witness Name, Other Vehicle, Description of Loss, and Vehicle Drivable all match the document text. One extracted field is incorrectly mapped: Date of Loss was extracted as "around noon," but the transcript uses that as the approximate time, not the date. Several expected FNOL fields are not present in the extraction, though many are also not stated in the transcript.

signal_credibility.findings: No signals were detected, but the transcript supports at least moderate claim complexity. There is clear third-party involvement with an unidentified hit-and-run vehicle, a police report, witness evidence, possible frame damage, and an explicit coverage decision point between collision coverage and identifying the adverse party first. No injury or legal escalation is stated, so those signal types are not required. The absence of any signal underrepresents the claim handling risk.

coverage_analysis.findings: The document raises a meaningful coverage handling issue: the insured wants to delay proceeding under collision coverage while the carrier attempts to identify the hit-and-run vehicle. This creates a potential first-party collision vs. third-party recovery decision, deductible recovery considerations, and possible rental timing implications. The transcript does not provide many standard intake demographics or vehicle identifiers, so those are document-level omissions rather than extraction failures.
gaps: Insured vehicle details (Vehicle Year, Vehicle Make, Vehicle Model, VIN, License Plate)

overall_validation.summary: The extraction is largely accurate, but it contains two semantic mapping errors: "around noon" is a time reference rather than a date, and "New Jersey plate" is not insurance information. The claim also has unsupported signal under-detection, particularly around coverage handling and damage severity.
recommended_actions: Correct Date of Loss by leaving it blank or unresolved unless a calendar date is found elsewhere.
Move "around noon" to Time of Loss if that field is supported in the schema.
Remove Other Vehicle Insurance unless actual carrier information is documented.
Add a coverage_issue signal for first-party collision versus third-party identification/recovery handling.
Consider a severity signal based on door intrusion, cracked window, and possible frame damage.
Obtain missing witness contact details and insured vehicle identifiers during follow-up.
